problem: Prior zero-shot object-goal navigation relies on dense 3D semantic maps, scene graphs or belief maps, while VLN/VLA models need large-scale training or fine-tuning; both lack a light interface that grounds VLM semantic reasoning into metric navigation goals.
motivation: Current VLMs are weak at 3D spatial reasoning but strong at 2D image reasoning. Frontiers are sparse, actionable and naturally encode exploration, so they could serve as semantic anchors. This would avoid dense semantic mapping and policy training.
key_idea: Detect visual frontiers in a single RGB image (FrontierNet), mark them with set-of-marks, ask a VLM for per-frontier goal-relevance probabilities that reweight the information gain, and manage the lifted 3D frontiers globally for zero-shot navigation.
insight: Doing detection and reasoning in the same 2D image space lets an off-the-shelf VLM be swapped freely: four VLMs, from LLaVA 1.6 to Gemini-2.5-flash, vary by at most 3% SR on HM3D. At a matched VLM, OpenFrontier (LLaVA 1.6: 74.2 SR) far exceeds UniGoal (54.5) and History-Aug. VLM (46.0), so the gain comes from the frontier representation rather than VLM strength. Combining the VLM semantic prior with FrontierNet's geometric information gain balances exploration and exploitation; failures are mainly false-positive detections and local minima of the point-goal policy.
method: Visual frontier detection: FrontierNet on a keyframe RGB (every 6 steps) gives frontier clusters with information gain g_hat, back-projected to 3D poses using pose and intrinsics.
Set-of-marks VLM reweighting: markers are drawn at frontier centroids, and one VLM query returns a probability p_i per frontier; utility g_i = p_i * g_hat_i.

Global frontier management: frontiers are merged (1.8 m), pruned when cleared, and chosen by u_i = g_i / distance to robot; stalled frontiers (15 steps) are dropped and cleared frontiers are recorded.

Viewpoint frontier and verification: SAM3 open-vocabulary segmentation plus depth gives an object centroid and an infinite-utility viewpoint frontier. After reaching it, the VLM verifies target presence (p>0.7) before final approach and termination.
Low-level execution: a pretrained DD-PPO PointNav policy (VLFM weights) in simulation; in the real world, a Wavemap occupancy grid from Metric3Dv2 depth with RRT* and pure pursuit.
Emergency rotation: artificial rotation frontiers, plus a relaxed gain threshold, handle views with no frontiers.
Optional history-augmented variant: recent keyframes are appended to the VLM query to lower relevance of already-seen areas (proof-of-concept, qualitative only).

setting.backbone: Gemini-2.5-flash (frozen VLM) + FrontierNet (pretrained) + SAM3 + DD-PPO PointNav (pretrained)
setting.training_data: none (training-free; uses pretrained FrontierNet, DD-PPO, SAM3 and VLMs)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with pose (sim); RGB with monocular depth (Metric3Dv2) and VIO pose (real)
setting.action_space: Habitat discrete actions (0.25 m forward, 30° turn) via a PointNav policy; continuous velocity via a pure-pursuit controller on the real robot
setting.simulator: Habitat 0.2.4 (HM3D, MP3D, OVON) + real Boston Dynamics Spot
setting.privileged: none (pose and camera intrinsics from the simulator)

numbers_note: Real-world: 70% SR over 10 trials on 5 objects (small-scale, not a benchmark).
results: Zero-shot OpenFrontier reaches 77.3 SR / 35.6 SPL on HM3D, above Uni-NaVid (fine-tuned, 73.7/37.1) in SR and far above BeliefMapNav (61.4/30.6). On MP3D it gets 40.7/17.8 (UniGoal 41.0 SR) and on OVON val-unseen 39.0/20.1 (Uni-NaVid 39.5 SR). Real-world Spot deployment achieved 70% success.
limitations: Poor failure recovery: false-positive detections, local minima of the DD-PPO point-goal policy and exhausted step budgets dominate failures, with no semantic-level replanning.
Termination and target verification are hard; some failures come from benchmark ground-truth ambiguity.
Real-world evaluation is small (10 trials), and simulation depends on API VLMs (Gemini) plus several pretrained modules.
